newsitem.title: UK: ACPC defends coffee export curbs.
newsitem.headline: ACPC defends coffee export curbs.

text.p: Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) on Wednesday defended its recent decision to extend export restrictions by 12 months from July 1, saying the action was taken after considering the needs of the markets.

The 14-member ACPC, led by Brazil, was responding to a statement by the European Coffee Federation (ECF) calling on producers to revoke their "unilateral" supply curbs or face the longer-term risk of a boom and bust cycle.

In a statement issued Wednesday after the ECF annual meeting in Vienna on Tuesday, the group said "in the longer term there is a risk of a boom-bust cycle' with alternating periods of very high and very low prices."
The London-based ACPC said the producers were well aware of the risk higher prices had over consumption levels.
"All their recent actions have been based on a sound analysis of the market fundamentals and the needs of the market," it said.

ACPC also repeated the statement it made on May 21 following the decision to continue with the curbs that "the priority of the established policy is to ensure prices remain at a level renumerative to producers, but allowing continuing growth in worldwide consumption of coffee."
In Wednesday's statement, ACPC said the recent market behaviour, especially the price rallies, should be confronted with the situation of the underlying market fundamentals.
"The fundamentals show an unprecedented level of annual exports, reaching over 80 million bags in the 12 months up to April this year, well above the level of consumption," it said.
"This allowed not only an increase in stocks held in consuming countries to the level of 10 million bags, as a recent estimate for April, but also a build up of working stocks by roasters," it added.

The grouping also said it looked forward to working with the ECF and all other institutions involved in the coffee sector to ensure stability of the coffee economy. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
